source_hashes.note: Derived from the D1 candidate frozen 2026-11-15. Six question texts and their rubric propositions were made team-neutral; no D1 facet, qualifier, priority or ID changed. Release 1.1.0 appended Modules 17-18 (63 questions, 129 facets).

question_manifest.question_text: What residential real-estate markets does your team actively serve? Identify primary cities/counties and secondary relocation markets.
What types of buyers currently make up your business? For example, first-time buyers, move-up buyers, relocations, investors, cash buyers, and returning clients.
Approximately what proportion of your buyer business comes from each major segment? Estimates are acceptable.
What languages does your team use for marketing, prospect communications, and appointments?
What is your primary value proposition to homebuyers? Why should a prospective buyer choose your team?
What problems or concerns usually motivate prospects to contact you?
Do different buyer types receive different onboarding, financing, or appointment processes?
Which prospect types tend to convert into active buyers, and which frequently stall?
What makes your team's buying experience meaningfully different from other agents' processes?
What buyer outcomes would you most like your system to improve, and how would you define measurable success?
List every active buyer lead source: paid Meta advertising, Facebook, Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, organic content, websites, referrals, seminars, open houses, database reactivation, or others.
Which sources currently generate the greatest lead volume?
For each major source, what exactly does the advertisement or content promise the viewer?
What action is the prospect instructed to take—submit a form, send a DM, comment a keyword, call, register, or book directly?
What information is requested before the prospect becomes a lead?
Do prospects expect a consultation, a list of homes, an affordability assessment, a financing conversation, an educational resource, or something else?
Are there important differences in intent between paid-social and organic-social leads?
Are any campaigns attracting people outside your service area or people who misunderstand your offer?
How are original source, campaign, ad, and subsequent interactions attributed in your CRM?
How much is spent per channel, and which marketing production/labor costs are tracked?
Which specific ads, hooks, videos, or offers seem to produce the most suitable prospects?
Are there documented differences between leads attracted by educational content, testimonials, property tours, and financing-related content?
What happens immediately after a prospect submits an inquiry?
How does that information enter the CRM currently in use?
Who receives the new lead, and how is that person selected?
Which VA or agent is responsible for the first contact?
What information can the assigned person see before contacting the prospect?
What happens if the assigned person is unavailable?
How are duplicate leads, existing contacts, past clients, or already represented buyers identified?
Are different lead sources prioritized differently?
How long does it usually take before a human makes the first meaningful outreach attempt?
What happens when a lead arrives outside normal coverage hours?
How do you detect unassigned, unworked, or incorrectly routed leads?
What fields, tags, stages, or triggers are currently used to organize different buyer types?
What are the exact responsibilities of each VA who handles buyer inquiries?
Are those VAs licensed or unlicensed, and who supervises their activities?
What is the first outreach method—telephone, SMS, WhatsApp, email, or another channel?
What is the exact opening script used when a new lead answers?
How does the VA establish relevance, explain the reason for calling, and gain permission to continue?
What qualifying or discovery questions are asked before offering an appointment?
How is the first appointment introduced and described?
What specific benefit does the VA tell the prospect they will receive from attending?
What is said when the prospect agrees to book?
What happens when the prospect says they are busy, just browsing, not ready, or unsure about purchasing?
What happens when the prospect does not answer the first call or text?
What is the actual follow-up sequence over subsequent days and weeks?
What causes the VA to stop contact, change strategy, escalate, or transfer the prospect?
Are appointments booked automatically, through a shared calendar, or manually?
How do you know whether the prospect understands what the appointment is for?
Are the appointment-setting scripts standardized, trained, monitored, and updated based on real conversations?
Which buyer questions repeatedly arise before the first appointment?
What qualifies a lead as cold, dormant, unresponsive, nurture-stage, or lost?
Who owns these leads—the original VA, assigned agent, another agent, or a dedicated reactivation role?
How are older lead lists assigned to agents?
What is the actual first reactivation script?
What information about the previous relationship is reviewed before calling?
How do agents determine whether the person's buying circumstances have changed?
What follow-up cadence is used, and does it vary by readiness and contact preference?
How are opt-outs, prior refusals, and channel permissions handled?
How is an appointment from reactivation attributed and recorded?
Do reactivated prospects follow the same first and second appointment structure?
Which prior reasons for delay are most commonly resolved before reactivation succeeds?
Who conducts appointment 1, and how is the responsible person assigned?
Is appointment 1 conducted by phone, video, or in person?
How much time generally passes between booking and the actual appointment?
What confirmation does the prospect receive immediately after booking?
What is the prospect told they need to prepare?
What educational resources, links, documents, or videos currently arrive before the meeting?
What reminders occur, through which channels, and at what times?
Who verifies that the prospect is still planning to attend?
What happens when a buyer cancels, requests to reschedule, or does not attend?
What are the most common known reasons for first-appointment no-shows?
What does the assigned agent wish every prospect understood before the appointment began?
What questions could a short educational video answer before appointment 1?
Walk me through the first five minutes. How does the agent greet the prospect?
How does the agent introduce themselves, the team, and the purpose of the appointment?
Is there an established agenda or script?
What is the prospect told will happen during the meeting and afterward?
What questions identify the prospect's reason for buying?
How are desired timing, urgency, and readiness established?
How are household needs and participating decision-makers discussed?
How does the agent learn which cities, property types, and features the buyer prefers?
What is asked about the buyer's desired monthly housing expenditure and purchase budget?
How are existing representation relationships identified?
What exactly does the agent teach about the overall homebuying process?
How is the team's role explained?
What proof or examples are presented to demonstrate competence?
Are compensation, buyer representation agreements, services, duration, and termination discussed? If so, how and when?
Are financing, credit, down payment, assistance programs, closing costs, or lender introductions discussed?
Are market conditions or available geographic options introduced?
What information or understanding must the agent obtain before ending the meeting?
Under what circumstances is appointment 2 offered?

What happens if the buyer refuses or postpones the second appointment?

How do different agents conduct this appointment differently?
What distinguishes appointments that progress from appointments that do not?
What would an exceptionally well-prepared buyer already know before joining this appointment?
At what stage is financing first discussed with the buyer?
Who introduces the lender or recommends obtaining preapproval?
Can buyers use their own lender, and how is that handled?
Who determines whether the prospect has been prequalified or preapproved?
Does lender contact occur before appointment 1, during it, afterward, or at another stage?
What does the buyer need to complete before the second appointment?
What specific lender information is communicated back to the licensed agent, and through what authorized process?
Who explains the difference between the maximum loan-supported purchase amount and the buyer's preferred spending limit?
How are down payments, cash-to-close, estimated monthly payments, taxes, insurance, HOA costs, and other ongoing ownership expenses addressed?
How is the buyer's financial comfort level documented without collecting unnecessary sensitive information?
What happens if a buyer is preapproved for more than they want to spend?
What happens if the desired location is not feasible within the buyer's chosen budget?
What happens if the lender cannot approve the buyer?
What happens when the lender is delayed or cannot obtain necessary information?
Is there a defined requalification or readiness-follow-up process?
What percentage of first-appointment buyers reach the second appointment with verified financing readiness?
Which financing-related misconceptions repeatedly consume agent appointment time?
What general financing concepts could be responsibly taught in advance without implying a specific loan approval?
What triggers the transition from appointment 1 to appointment 2?
How soon is appointment 2 usually scheduled?
Who owns the prospect during the interval?
What communications does the prospect receive immediately after appointment 1?
Are there educational materials, financing tasks, questionnaires, property examples, or other assignments?
Who checks whether those tasks are completed?
What prerequisites must be met before appointment 2 proceeds?
What exactly is appointment 2 promised to accomplish?
What happens if the buyer does not complete financing tasks?
What happens if the buyer stops responding?
Are reminders different from those used for appointment 1?
What causes buyers to lose interest between appointments?
What information do agents repeatedly have to explain at the beginning of appointment 2?
What would the ideal buyer understand before joining appointment 2?
What preparation could help a buyer evaluate realistic alternatives without feeling pressured?
Who conducts appointment 2, and who else normally attends?
What are the prerequisites?
What software is used for the live video meeting?

What maps, listings, screen shares, or visual aids are used?
How are property type, condition, size, commute, expenses, and other buyer priorities considered?

What does the agent say when the buyer's preferred area is outside their spending range?

What concerns do buyers raise about moving farther from their first-choice area?
Which alternative markets are most frequently rejected, and why?
Is there a formal presentation or is the meeting conversational?
What sequence does the agent follow?

Are homes compared side by side?
How are misunderstandings, uncertainty, disappointment, or hesitation handled?
Which objections occur most often?
How do you distinguish a buyer who needs more education from one who genuinely does not want the available options?
What exact decision do you want the buyer to make by the end of appointment 2?
What conditions determine readiness to schedule tours?
What exact language is used to invite the buyer to see homes?
What is said about representation, required agreements, services, and compensation?
Who selects or approves the first property list?
How is the first tour date established?
What information is recorded before the appointment ends?
What happens if the buyer likes the process but does not want to tour?
Why do some second appointments end without a next step?
What would the best-prepared buyer already understand before this meeting?
At what stage do you consider someone a buyer client rather than merely a lead?
At what point are buyer representation agreements introduced, explained, and signed?
How are the agreement's services, term, compensation, and termination provisions discussed?
Who verifies that all required disclosures and agreements are completed before applicable services or tours?
Who creates the buyer's initial property list?
How are the buyer's preferences recorded and transferred to the showing agent?
Who coordinates property availability and scheduling?
Who conducts the tour?
What does the buyer receive before their first showing?
What happens when approved properties are no longer available?
How are buyers who change budget, geographic preference, or timing handled?
How often do buyers agree to tour but fail to schedule or attend?
Are buyers handed off between agents? If so, how is continuity maintained?
What happens when the buyer decides not to proceed?
What preparation would make the first tour more useful for both buyer and agent?
What are the ten most common buyer questions across the entire funnel?
What are the ten most common reasons buyers hesitate or decline to continue?
At which stage does each commonly appear?
What exact words do buyers use when raising those concerns?
How does the team currently respond?
Which concerns are informational misunderstandings?
Which concerns reflect genuine financing, affordability, timing, geographic, or household constraints?
Which concerns are about the agent's value, representation terms, or trust?
Which objections recur after the team believes they were already answered?
What reasons are logged for lost or deferred buyers?
What happens when a buyer chooses another agent or lender?
How are prospects who legitimately are not ready placed into appropriate future follow-up?
Which questions could be answered accurately through reusable videos?
What proof, demonstration, or explanation has actually helped buyers understand the process?

What does each of the four agents own?
What does each VA own?
Which roles conduct appointment 1 and appointment 2?

Who owns prospect follow-up after each appointment?
Who has authority to change a lead stage, reassign a lead, or close an opportunity?
What happens if the assigned agent or VA is absent?
What training is provided to VAs and agents?
How is script adherence or consultation quality evaluated?
Are calls or meetings reviewed with appropriate recording permissions?
What performance reports does each person receive?
Which handoffs most frequently fail?
How is available capacity measured?
Who is responsible for supervising unlicensed activities?
Which repetitive explanations currently consume significant licensed-agent time?
What CRM and connected communication systems are currently in use?
What are the active buyer pipeline stages?
What triggers entry into and exit from each stage?
Which tasks and messages are automated?
Which actions still require manual execution?
Who maintains and approves CRM changes?
How are appointment bookings, cancellations, reschedules, and attendance recorded?
How is lender readiness captured without exposing unnecessary confidential data?
How are lead owners, backups, and overdue tasks monitored?
What happens when a prospect replies to an automated sequence?
How are marketing opt-outs and communication preferences enforced?
How are duplicate messages and conflicting automation triggers prevented?
Are any current pipeline numbers known to be inaccurate?
Can the system deliver different educational assets based on the buyer's stage?
Can video delivery and meaningful engagement be tracked?
What automation capabilities exist but are not currently used?
What period and source cohorts can be reviewed reliably?
How many unique buyer leads entered each major source cohort?
How many were valid and suitable?

How many produced two-way conversations?
How many booked appointment 1?
How many appointment 1 meetings were due and actually held?
How many progressed to appointment 2?
How many appointment 2 meetings were due and held?
How many obtained verified financing readiness?
How many signed representation agreements?
How many scheduled and completed their first tour?
How long did prospects take to progress between stages?
How many are still active or pending rather than lost?
How do these measures differ by lead source and responsible agent?
What does the team spend on advertising, content production, VA labor, appointment labor, CRM, and related acquisition activities?
What mature-cohort offer, contract, and closing data are available?
Is retained contribution after applicable compensation splits and variable costs measured?
Are the available reports accurate enough to calculate stage conversion, or do we first need a data-quality assessment?
Which specific operational targets has the owner established for lead response, appointments, qualified buyers, and closings?
Which educational videos, social posts, presentations, PDFs, and checklists already exist?
When are they shown or sent?
Which are specific to appointment 1?
Which are specific to appointment 2?
Who creates and approves buyer education?
Which buyer questions are already covered adequately by existing material?
Which recurring explanations are missing?
What client testimonials, case studies, process demonstrations, and other genuine proof are available with appropriate usage permissions?
Do agents consistently reference or reinforce educational assets during appointments?
Can prospects access the information easily on their preferred device and in their preferred language?
What information should a buyer understand before appointment 1?
What different information should a buyer understand before appointment 2?
Which questions require individualized advice and should not be delegated to prerecorded content?
Are there important buyer-segment variations that would require different explanations?
In the last 12 months, about how many buyer deals closed, and about how much commission did they bring in before anyone was paid?
After agent splits, referral fees, brokerage fees and other per-deal costs, about how much does the team keep from a typical buyer closing?
For a recent stretch of months, about how much was spent to win buyer clients, and about how many of the leads from that same stretch have since signed or closed?
In the last 12 months, about how many buyer closings came from repeat past clients, and how many came from referrals by past clients?
What commission rate or fee does the team charge buyers, does it vary by buyer type, and about what is the average purchase price?

When did the buyer fee last change and what happened to sign-ups afterward, do buyers pay any admin or transaction fee, and how often does the team reduce commission or give a rebate to win or keep a buyer?
Does the amount the team keeps per deal differ by lead source, price range or agent, and roughly how?
After every business cost, including the owner's pay if taken, about how much did the business keep last year?
Does the team track cost per lead, per held appointment and per closing, overall or by source, and which lead count is used?
How long does it usually take from a buyer lead's first contact until the commission check arrives?
Does any money come in during a buyer client's first 30 days, or is everything paid at closing, and how is marketing paid for while waiting?
Counting every past buyer client, about how many deals has the average client done with the team, including later purchases and sales?
About how many past clients are in the database, how many could still be reached today, how many heard from the team in the last 6 months, and how many are known to have used another agent since?
After closing, how often does a past client hear from the team personally, what is done, and about how much does it cost per year?
About what share of closed buyers left a review or testimonial, and what share sent at least one referral?

Besides the purchase, what other income has come from buyer clients, such as listing the home they left, a later sale, an investment purchase, rentals or referral fees the law allows, and roughly how many clients produced each?
What happens to leads who are not ready to buy yet, and of not-ready leads from a year or more ago, about how many later bought with the team?

Of buyers who sign with the team, about how many drop out before closing and why, how many go quiet for two weeks or more first, and when a buyer wants to stop, does anyone talk with them and about how many stay?
Thinking of the best 10–20% of past clients by commission plus repeat and referral business, what do they have in common?
Is there a step after which buyers become much more likely to close, such as preapproval or a first tour within a certain number of days?

How many buyer clients can one agent handle at a time, about how many closings does an agent do per year, and roughly what share of an agent's week goes to appointments and tours, follow-up, prospecting, and admin and training?
What revenue or closings goal does the owner have for the next 12 months?
If twice as many leads came in tomorrow, where would things break first, and which stage loses the most people in the team's own numbers?
Which would change the business most if it improved: more leads, more leads becoming clients, more money per client, more repeat and referral business, or depending less on any one person or source?
Which of these money numbers come from real reports, and which are the owner's best estimate?
Besides splits and fees, about how much does it cost the team to serve one buyer from signing to closing, such as showing time, a transaction coordinator, mileage, gifts or per-client software?
How does the team pay for leads and marketing before commission arrives, and about how many months of current spending could it cover with no closings?
What do the team's ads or lead forms offer people for getting in touch, and which offer brings the most leads and which brings the most closings?

From first contact to closing, what else does the team offer a buyer and in what order, such as a lender introduction, listing their current home, moving help or other referrals the law allows, and about how many said yes to each last year?
When a buyer declines the buyer agreement, is anything else offered, such as a shorter or single-property agreement, fewer services for a lower fee or listing alerts only, and about how many accept?
How long does the buyer agreement run, how can a buyer end it early, is a fee owed if they do, and is any fee waived for buyers who commit?
Does the team offer different service levels or a package price for buying and selling together, and about what share of clients chose each?
Do past clients get a credit, discount or bonus on their next deal, and does any client bring in recurring income such as property management or investor services, and about how much per year?
How many calls and texts does a new lead who doesn't answer get, over how many days, before moving to long-term follow-up?
Of calls to new leads, about how many get answered?
On which days and hours can a buyer book appointment 1, and how many start times are offered per hour?
About how many first appointments happen the same day the lead is reached, or get moved earlier?
When a booked buyer texts a question, about how long until someone replies, and is that tracked?
Does the team grade leads, about what share fall in each grade, and who gets the best ones?
Is anyone paid for appointments that actually happen, and how much compared with their pay per closing?

Of buyers who didn't move forward last quarter, about how many gave each reason, such as timing, money, a spouse or partner, wanting a different area, approach or agent, needing to think, or a bad past experience?
How often is a decision-maker missing from appointment 2, and what happens then?
In the last 12 months, how many agents and VAs joined, and how many left?
Which calls are recorded and kept, about how many were reviewed together last month, how are calls picked for review, and how often does each person's call get reviewed?
About how many new ads or ad versions are made per month, at what monthly spend did costs start climbing if spending was raised, and are the ad click rate and click-to-lead rate known?
Does the team keep a ranked list of its best ads or posts by leads or appointments, and does it track or test ad opening lines and calls to action?
About what share of the team's ads and posts feature the owner, versus agents or clients?
On which review sites does the team have reviews, about how many with what average rating, how many new ones arrive per month, when was the latest, and is a satisfaction score collected?
About how many social followers and email contacts does the team have?
How many client or past-client events does the team hold per year?
Which client-result numbers does the team keep, such as buyers helped per year, average days from signing to keys, or first-time buyers helped?
When does the team stop running an ad, how much and how fast is budget raised on an ad that works, and what share of new ads are new versions of ads that already worked?
Are ads judged mainly by cost per lead or by the appointments and closings they produce, and about how much commission is one held first appointment worth?
Have the team's best organic posts been run as paid ads and how did they do, and are separate versions made for each placement?
About how many hours a week do agents or VAs spend calling or texting leads who haven't booked, about how many appointments does an hour produce, and at what time of day do leads answer most?
If a booked buyer never replies to confirmations, is the appointment kept, cancelled or rebooked, and about how often does that happen?
When a buyer no-shows or says no, how long does the team keep contacting them, and about what share of the last 2 months' no-shows and no's has been contacted again?
Do agents ask for referrals at signing or at closing, and about what share of clients are asked?
Of buyers who sign, about how many decide during appointment 2 versus after later follow-up, and when appointment 2 ends without a decision, how often is the next meeting booked before it ends?
About how long do appointment 1 and appointment 2 usually last, and is there a set time limit?
How long after starting does a new VA or agent take a first live call or appointment, and what must they show or pass first?
How often does the owner or a team lead meet one-on-one with each VA and agent, and how often does the team train together?
Is there a written weekly or monthly standard for each role, and what happens when someone falls below it?
